items.followUp: A solution contains 8 g of salt in 200 cm³ of solution. Calculate its percentage mass/volume concentration.

rubric.why: Assesses the definition of percentage mass/volume concentration.
rubric.description: States the mass of solute, in grams, present in 100 cm³ of solution.
rubric.how: Award for relating the mass of solute to 100 cm³ of solution.

rubric.why: Assesses a correct example of percentage mass/volume concentration.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as 5 g of salt in 100 cm³ of solution, or identifies it as 5% mass/volume.
rubric.how: Award for a valid example that correctly relates the solute mass to the solution volume.

modelAnswer: Percentage mass/volume is the mass of solute, in grams, dissolved in 100 cm3 of solution.
For example, a solution containing 5 g of salt in 100 cm3 of solution has a concentration of 5% mass/volume.

items.followUp: Write the equation for the reaction of methane with chlorine in diffused sunlight and name the type of reaction.

rubric.why: Assesses the reaction type and its stated condition.
rubric.description: States that chlorine substitutes for a hydrogen atom in methane in diffused sunlight.
rubric.how: Award for identifying substitution and mentioning diffused sunlight.

rubric.why: Assesses the products of the reaction.
rubric.description: Identifies chloromethane and hydrogen chloride as products.
rubric.how: Award for both products, whether given by name or in the reaction equation.

modelAnswer: In diffused sunlight, chlorine substitutes for one hydrogen atom in methane.
The products are chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.

items.followUp: Define empirical formula and give the empirical formula of glucose, C6H12O6, and magnesium chloride, MgCl2.

rubric.why: Assesses the definition of empirical formula.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound, or ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is a simplest whole-number ratio and identifying the particles whose ratio is represented.

rubric.why: Assesses the explanation for a covalent compound.
rubric.description: Explains that a covalent compound's empirical formula gives the simplest atom ratio and can differ from its molecular formula; glucose has empirical formula CH2O.
rubric.how: Award for the correct glucose empirical formula or a correct explanation of how the empirical and molecular formulas relate.

rubric.why: Assesses the explanation for an ionic compound.
rubric.description: Explains that an ionic empirical formula shows the simplest ratio of ions; MgCl2 represents a 1:2 ratio.
rubric.how: Award for the correct ionic formula or the correct simplest ion ratio.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound; for an ionic compound, it represents the simplest ratio of ions in its formula unit.
For a covalent compound, the empirical formula may differ from the molecular formula. For example, glucose has molecular formula C6H12O6 and empirical formula CH2O.
For an ionic compound, the formula gives the simplest ratio of ions. For example, MgCl2 represents a 1:2 ratio of magnesium ions to chloride ions.
